API reference

Import from src/index.js.

createEdy(options)

container is a host element. Optional locale is en or es (default en); theme is light, dark, or system (default system); services is a host capability object; and extensions is an array. Instances expose async start(), activateExtension(id), deactivateExtension(id), and dispose(). Expanded mode fills the browser viewport rather than invoking native browser fullscreen; Escape restores it.

logo is an optional non-empty image URL string for the header, resolved relative to the host page when relative. Each instance can use a different logo; if omitted, Edy loads its bundled SVG from src/assets/edy-logo.svg. The image is decorative beside the retained Edy text. Its source and licensing note are recorded in src/assets/CREDITS.md.

Extension context

  • commands.register(id, { label, execute, enabled }), execute(id, ...args), refresh().
  • views.register(id, { title, location, icon, render, viewport }), open(id).
  • documents.open(id, { title, render }), close(id).
  • menus.register(menuId, { id, label, commandId, icon, shortcut, order }). Built-in groups include file, edit, view, help and context.
  • status.register(id, { label, tooltip, onClick, commandId }).
  • notifications.info(message), success(message), error(error, message).
  • ui.confirm(message) returns a promise of a boolean.
  • services, subscriptions, locale, translate, extensionId, and apiVersion.

For renderers that attach listeners or own frames, return { element, dispose }. Edy disposes the contribution when it is unmounted. A closed document is removed; closing a sidebar or preview hides the surface.

UI helpers

Exports include createButton, createLink, createBadge, createMessage, createProgress, createSeparator, createForm, createList, createTabs, createButtonGroup, createAccordion, openDialog, confirmDialog and createPreviewFrame. See the JSDoc in src/ui/controls.js for their parameters and src/extensions/demo.js for working form, tree and preview examples.

createForm supports native color, date, range, switch, and other standard fields, plus the icon and tinymce fields:

createForm({
  translate: context.translate,
  onError: (error) => context.notifications.error(error),
  fields: [
    { name: 'icon', label: 'Icon', type: 'icon', value: 'star', options: [
      { value: 'star', label: 'Star', width: 24, height: 24, path: 'M12 2 L15 9 L22 9 L17 14 L19 22 L12 18 L5 22 L7 14 L2 9 L9 9 Z' },
    ] },
    { name: 'content', label: 'Content', type: 'tinymce', mode: 'simple', value: '<p>Hello</p>' },
  ],
  onSubmit: ({ icon, content }) => console.log(icon, content),
});

Icon options contain a string value and label and an SVG path with its view box width and height. The example extension configures a selection from Font Awesome Free. The icon field submits the chosen value; TinyMCE submits HTML. Treat submitted HTML as untrusted and sanitize it before rendering.

TinyMCE modes are simple (default), full (general open-source plugins), and custom. The simple toolbar includes undo/redo, blocks, bold, italic, underline, left/center/right/justified alignment, and clear formatting. Pass TinyMCE settings through options, for example { mode: 'custom', options: { plugins: 'lists link', toolbar: 'bold | link' } }. The field owns target, selector, and readonly. The default license key is gpl; the host is responsible for compliance or supplying its own license_key. TinyMCE runs in a same-origin iframe to avoid its unsupported Shadow DOM integration. The iframe follows the editor's height when it is resized, including by keyboard or automatic resizing. The form rejects submissions until initialization finishes; load failures are reported through onError (or console.error). TinyMCE's own interface defaults to English; provide a local language pack through its language and language_url options to localize it. The static build includes the TinyMCE runtime. When deploying src/ directly, also deploy node_modules/tinymce/ beside it. The example additionally requires node_modules/@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons/. See the packages' license files for their terms and attribution.

createList(items, { tree: true, onSelect }) renders a keyboard-operable tree with collapsible branches. List and tree items may include an optional icon string, rendered decoratively before their label:

createList([
  { id: 'src', label: 'src', icon: '📁', children: [
    { id: 'index', label: 'index.html', icon: '📄' },
  ] },
], { tree: true, onSelect: (item) => console.log(item.id) });

openDialog accepts a title, DOM content, close label and host container, while createButtonGroup groups labeled actions. These controls are demonstrated in the sample extension. When the dialog content is a form returned by createForm, its close button is placed in the form's action row next to the form buttons. Other dialog content retains a separate close button.

For example, an extension can render a validated form:

import { createForm } from './src/index.js';

// Inside activate(context):
context.views.register('settings', {
  title: 'Settings',
  location: 'editor',
  render: () => createForm({
    translate: context.translate,
    fields: [
      { name: 'title', label: 'Title', required: true },
      { name: 'enabled', label: 'Enabled', type: 'checkbox', value: true },
    ],
    onSubmit: (values) => context.notifications.info(values.title),
  }),
});

Preview frame

createPreviewFrame({ src, title, allowedOrigin, sandbox, operations, validateMessage }) returns { element, postMessage, onMessage, dispose }. onMessage returns a disposable subscription. postMessage accepts an object with an allowed operation and optional object payload; outgoing messages are limited to 64 KiB. See live preview.
